rows: Each polygon has a separate Land Registry-INSPIRE ID and polygons are split by local authority; boundary polygons may appear in both authority files.
Exact identifier and source-authority generation binding are required.
HMLR polygons are captured against British National Grid and reprojection can shift features by up to 15 metres.
Native CRS or a receipted high-quality transform is required.
The current package was published 5 July 2026 and is replaced on the first Sunday monthly.
Current catalogue availability does not prove the exact downloaded and parsed GML bytes.
HMLR describes polygon identifiers and records all polygon data against British National Grid.
The matcher must not substitute a generic feature identifier for the intended polygon identity.
Transformer exposes accuracy and area_of_use and supports allow_ballpark and only_best controls.
Default transformation selection is not an accuracy receipt.
CRS objects expose authority, axis and area-of-use metadata.
A textual CRS parse alone does not prove the expected native CRS contract.
PROJ network and data context affect transformation availability and operation selection.
Runtime transformation resources and network policy need explicit receipts.
make_valid can repair invalid geometry and may produce complex results depending on method.
Repairs need before/after type, area, component and hash evidence.
covers returns true when no point of the second geometry lies outside the first, including boundary coverage semantics.
A status labelled strictly inside needs an explicit interior predicate policy.
Validity is a geometry predicate separate from finite-coordinate, bounds and business-area checks.
Valid type alone is insufficient for accepted HMLR geometry.
Fiona collections expose driver, schema, CRS and layer controls.
The effective driver and schema should be pinned and receipted.
Fiona relies on OGR drivers and publishes a tested supported-driver set.
Installed driver availability is not equivalent to an application allowlist.
GML support depends on the Fiona/GDAL build and linked native libraries.
Runtime native-library and driver versions affect parser behaviour.
The generic GML driver can infer feature classes when an XSD is absent, and documentation calls this approach error-prone.
Application-schema identity must be required for fail-closed matching.
GMLAS is driven by XML application schemas and maps GML through schema-aware processing.
Schema resources and network resolution policy must be pinned.
GDAL exposes many vector drivers with different parsing behaviours.
A datasource suffix does not by itself select the intended parser.
GMLAS can expose schema and field metadata including XML base types.
Layer and identifier field contracts can be checked before feature iteration.
The default decoder accepts NaN and Infinity and repeated names are not a strict schema policy.
Strict duplicate and non-finite rejection is required.
Path.resolve normalizes and resolves symbolic links where supported.
Final-handle containment on Windows remains a separate requirement.
hashlib computes digests over the exact bytes supplied.
A digest computed after parsing does not establish read-byte identity without a stable handle.
argparse converts command-line values but does not impose application-specific safe ranges.
max-files and resource limits require explicit validation.
os.replace supports atomic replacement under the filesystem contract.
Durability and generation-manifest binding remain separate.
Windows can return the final normalized path for an opened handle.
The handle must be opened under the intended reparse policy.
JSON object names should be unique and JSON numbers exclude NaN and Infinity.
Interoperable evidence documents should reject ambiguous and non-standard values.
